title: "1. Import data"

This script reads the two workbooks, adds years since diagnosis to the RUSH-era cohort, and makes the text categories into factors numbered as the original code numbered them. It produces `study_wide` and `control_wide`, one row per patient, for [2. Build long data](02_build_long_data.qmd) and [3. Paired comparisons](03_paired_comparisons.qmd).

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/01_import_data.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/01_import_data.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/01_import_data.R")
```

## Merge years since diagnosis

Join the two by patient number. The original code used `merge 1:1`, which keeps every row of both files, matched or not, and then tabulated how many matched (`tab _merge`). `full_join()` keeps every row the same way. Before the join, `check_unique_patients()` stops if a patient number appears twice in either file, as Stata's `1:1` does; `relationship = "one-to-one"` alone would check only the matched rows, so a repeated patient missing from the other file would get through. The control sheet gets the same check, standing in for the check Stata's `reshape …, i(PatientNumber)` made: a repeated row would add rows to the patient's stratum and break the four-row rule for the era comparison. The two marker columns exist only to count matched and unmatched patients, which is printed for the analyst and not saved.

Keeping unmatched patients is the original code's choice; a patient with no years-since-diagnosis value simply drops out of the models that use it.

```{r}
#| label: merge-years-since-diagnosis
#| eval: false
```

It gets the same cleaning, so its sex and age group are factors too.
